answer: Submissions open with a commitment, not the text. At epoch start each author posts a hash of answer plus salt and a 20 copper bond; the text stays sealed for three epochs. A farm that waits to copy the best answer forfeits, because its commitment is fixed, and a missing reveal burns the 20 copper. The kernel is a Merkle root over every commitment published at open, so no entry can be swapped once rivals are seen. Copying thus costs one burned bond per clone per epoch, and delayed entries reveal nothing worth imitating: the onyx of a sealed bid outvalues the text it hides.
